I am here to join the chorus of people that are here to dunk on VTI.

VTI’s underlying index, the CRSP Total US Stock Market, doesn’t have a profitability filter. So you are dragging the 40 percent of investable small caps that have never been profitable. This explains the performance lag it has to VOO.

VTI doesn’t have a seasoning requirement for IPOs, so it buys these small cap IPOs five days in when they are at their high, only to have them drawdown 20-50 percent over the next year.

VTI reconstitutes on a very public schedule that gets front run by the market every time. So it is always buying into strength and selling into weakness. This can create up to a 20 bps per year drag on returns.

VTI’s ten largest holdings are 34 percent compared to VOO’s 39 percent. So you are not really avoiding concentration risk.

VTI has more volatility than VOO because of all of the unprofitable small caps.

DFUS solves most of these problems. It is still market cap weighted though so is almost as concentrated at VTI.

For a less concentrated total us market, you can do AVUS. It is factor weighted. It will lag when the current leadership is surging and over perform when it takes a breather. We would need to see a full business cycle to see how meaningful factor weighting is.

Simple equities portion of the portfolio.

AVGV world value core 60 percent

SPMO (or the momentum ETF of your choice) 20 percent.

SCHD 20 percent

SPMO and SCHD only have a .67 correlation to each other, which is pretty low for equity to equity correlation.

Quarterly rebalance will create a bar bell effect that still has better growth than the market with a little smoother ride.

AVUV over long periods of time beats all of those and is predicted to outperform VOO and VTI for awhile. 

Understanding small cap value is important. Understanding value premium is important and that was omitted. 🙈

While VTI and chill is a great strategy, it would be better to add international and have 30-50% international exposure for long periods to have better diversification. 

Why else should people include Intl exposure? There are entire decades where the world has outperformed the US.
